properties.name: Perseverance Landing Ellipse
properties.description: This flat stretch of crater floor is where NASA's Perseverance rover landed on February 18, 2021, at a site now called Octavia E. Butler Landing. The ground is made of volcanic rock rich in olivine and pyroxene. It is a safe, well-studied place to begin the walk.

properties.name: Delta Front Climb
properties.description: The first 1.9 km from the landing site is nearly flat. Then the ground rises about 53 m, roughly the height of a 15-story building, at the edge of the delta. The delta is a raised fan of river sediment above the old lake floor, and this edge is where it drops down to the crater floor, like a curb but far bigger. Coming from the crater floor, the astronaut must climb it in a heavy suit over rough terrain, while energy may already be low and conditions on Mars can change.

properties.name: Western Delta Deposit
properties.description: Around 3.5 billion years ago, a river flowed into a lake inside Jezero and built this fan-shaped delta. Its layered rocks hold clays and carbonates, minerals that form in water and are good at preserving traces of ancient life. This is the most important science stop on the route.

properties.name: Western Breach
properties.description: This is where the ancient river broke into the crater and poured into the lake. The river carried rocks from the crater rim and beyond, so this spot samples a much wider area than the crater floor. Astronauts can collect a diverse set of rocks here in one place.
